doc.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Birth, parents and father's motel
summary: Marsalis gives his birth, his parents' origins and his father's motel business in Jefferson Parish.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My names Ellis Louis Marsalis, Jr. I was born in New Orleans, November 14, 1934.
Your birthday’s coming up in a few days.
Right.
Wonderful. 1934. Could you give us the names of your parents, please?
Ellis Louis Marsalis, Sr. My mother’s name was Florence Robinson Marsalis.
So Robinson was her maiden name.
Right.
Louis – the spelling of Louis – is it L-o-u-?
L-o-u-i-s.
Okay, good. Your father, where was he born?
He was born in Summit, Mississippi.
And your mother?
New Roads, Louisiana.
Were they married – were they in New Orleans – prior to your birth, obviously. Do you know when they arrived in New Orleans?

No, not exactly. Let’s see. I think my father when he was, I think, about 13, because my grandfather – his father – he worked on the L&N Railroad as a fireman. I’m not sure when my mother came, because she came from New Roads to New Orleans, but the year, I don’t know. They didn’t talk a lot about that.
What was your father’s occupation?
He did a lot of different things. Eventually he got this idea of starting a motel, which was right after the Second World War. He functioned with that until he retired from it.
So he ran a hotel. Where was the hotel located?
In an adjoining parish, Jefferson Parish. It was on River Road.
So, knowing American history at this time, it would have been segregated?
Right.
